title: Hubble Interacting Galaxy NGC 5754
caption: Interacting galaxies NGC 5754 and NGC 5752 (Arp 297), imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 5754, NGC 5752, NGC 5752/4, Arp 297 · constellation Boötes · about 200 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and W. Keel (University of Alabama, Tuscaloosa)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: A large spiral, NGC 5754, fills the right side of the frame, while its smaller companion, NGC 5752, sits in the bottom left corner. Together they make up the interacting pair Arp 297, some 200 million light-years away in Boötes, the Herdsman.

The two have responded to their encounter in very different ways. The big spiral's internal structure is barely disturbed. Signs of the interaction show up instead in tidal features around its outskirts, in the symmetry of its inner spiral pattern and in arms that kink just beyond an inner ring.

NGC 5752 has been changed far more. It has gone through a starburst, an intense episode of star formation, and a rich crowd of massive, luminous star clusters now gathers around its core, threaded with intricate lanes of dust. NASA attributes the contrast between the two galaxies to their different masses and sizes, so the same encounter has left one nearly intact and transformed the other.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 took this image. NASA has not published which filters were used or how colors were assigned.
understand.eye: The total exposure of 1.4 hours gathers far more light than the eye can collect in a single glance.

explore: Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 took this picture in 1999, years before NASA's 2008 anniversary release included it among 59 images of interacting and merging galaxies at many different stages of collision.
alt: A large spiral galaxy on the right and a smaller, clumpy companion galaxy with dust lanes in the bottom left corner.
